ModMetaData.name: RimMandrake Fluid Canals
ModMetaData.author: Mandrake
ModMetaData.description:
Dig a channel, let a fluid flow into it: a species- and biome-agnostic engine for canals that carry water, ooze, slime, oil, tar or fuel from a source into the terrain a colonist chooses.
Depth is the primitive. Every excavated cell carries two small integers — D, how far below the surface it was dug (shallow, mid, deep, SUPERDEEP), and F, how much liquid is in it — and everything else is a function of those two on one cell: what it costs to cross, how much it holds, and which liquid surface is drawn. We dig down; we never build up. There is no elevation model, no height advantage, and no fluid simulation: liquid levels itself out on a pulse, by sorting the deepest cells first and letting a full one overflow into whatever has room.
A natural liquid body IS a source — deep terrain that is already full, which is why it spills into a shallower channel dug at its edge. Liquid stays in what has been excavated.
Shipped: the depth/fill grid and its pulse engine (`RM_MapComponent_Excavation`), a dig designator that deepens a cell each time it is used, depth-derived movement cost, a three-tier fill ladder on vanilla's own edge-aware water ramps, and a `FluidDef` describing what a source carries. Water is the one liquid this pass, proving genericity.
Not yet built, and named so nobody thinks they are missing: filling a channel back in, sluice gates, sinks, ladders, fall-in capture at SUPERDEEP (until it exists, pawns will not path into a SUPERDEEP cell at all), burning liquids, irrigation, and per-source stock accounting. Requires Odyssey.
